坐姿，將樂器穩定持於身前。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或改變有效弦長以控制音: Sit and hold the instrument steady in front of the body. Hold the instrument steady in front of the body. The left hand stops the string or changes its sounding length to control the pitch; the right hand sets the string vibrating. A string instrument makes sound by passing the string's vibration into a soundbox, which amplifies it. Bow evenly, using the weight of the arm rather than the strength of the wrist.

椰胡可於廣東、福建、台灣、新加坡與馬來西亞等地的傳統音樂場合聆聽。它常見於廣東音: The yehu can be heard in traditional music settings in Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia. It is common in the accompaniment of Guangdong music, Cantonese ballads (yue'ou), Cantonese opera and dishui nanyin, and it is the leading instrument in Chaozhou music and is used to accompany Chaozhou zheng pieces; in Cantonese opera, Cantonese song and Chaozhou music it is often the second huqin. In Hakka mountain songs, Hakka bayin and Hakka opera it is an important characteristic accompanying instrument, usually paired with the kezixian, which Hakka speakers call the 'second string'. Beiguan, gezi music and opera sometimes use the wuxian in place of the daguanxian, again as the second huqin. In traditional Chaozhou solo playing and in the accompaniment of Chaozhou xianshi or Chaozhou zheng pieces only one note may be played per bow stroke, and slurring is forbidden.
椰胡屬弓弦樂器，琴筒以椰子殼製成，面板為桐木，琴馬為貝殼製。另有來源提到演奏端切: The yehu is a bowed instrument. Its soundbox is made from a coconut shell, the soundboard is paulownia, and the bridge is shell. Another source mentions that the playing end is cut open and covered with a piece of coconut wood, unlike the snakeskin usual on the erhu and gaohu; players mostly prefer silk strings rather than the steel strings common on the modern erhu. The bow hair passes between the two strings. The source does not state the materials of the remaining parts — neck, fingerboard, bow stick and so on.
椰胡是流行於廣東、福建、台灣及新加坡、馬來西亞等地的弓弦樂器，屬中國胡琴家族，又: The yehu is a bowed instrument popular in Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia, a member of the Chinese huqin family, also called the kezixian or wuxian. Its soundbox is a coconut shell, the soundboard is paulownia and the bridge is shell; the bow hair passes between the two strings, silk strings are usual, and the timbre is low and full. It accompanies Guangdong music, Cantonese ballads, Cantonese opera and dishui nanyin, can take the lead in Chaozhou music, and is an important instrument in Hakka mountain songs, Hakka bayin, Hakka opera and in beiguan and gezi music.
椰胡起源於廣東地區，是中國傳統弓弦樂器中獨具特色的樂器。以椰子殼為琴筒、桐木為面: The yehu originated in Guangdong and is a distinctive instrument among Chinese bowed strings. The combination of coconut-shell soundbox, paulownia soundboard and shell bridge gives it its particular low, full timbre. With the growth of Cantonese culture the yehu became an important accompanying instrument in Guangdong music, Cantonese ballads, Cantonese opera and other traditional arts.
椰胡音色低沉渾厚，具有溫潤而蒼勁的質感，帶有獨特的滄桑感。其音域主要集中在中低音: The yehu's timbre is low and full, warm yet sinewy, with a particular sense of weathered age. Its range lies mainly in the middle and lower register; the tone is full and deep and carries well. Because the soundbox is a coconut shell it has a natural resonating chamber and produces a sound that is warm without losing clarity. Next to the bright sharpness of the gaohu and the soft sweetness of the erhu, the yehu sounds more sinewy and archaic, more marked by folk character and history. Its resonance is distinctive and makes the most of the lower register, which is why it is indispensable in Cantonese music, Chaozhou music and Hakka music, and especially good at sustaining a dark mood and folk feeling.
經過長期的文化交流與傳播，椰胡的使用範圍不斷擴大。在福建、台灣、新加坡、馬來西亞: Through long cultural exchange and transmission the yehu's range of use has kept growing. It circulates widely in Minnan culture areas such as Fujian, Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia, and plays an important part in local musical forms. In Hakka music especially it works together with the erxian as the characteristic accompanying instrument of Hakka mountain songs, bayin and Hakka opera. In Chaozhou music it is regarded as the leading instrument, which shows its musical value fully. With Chinese migration it has gradually become a national instrument across regions, widely used in beiguan, gezi opera and other forms, and an important vehicle of traditional Chinese musical culture.
